content: Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of etravirine by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. Caution is advised, and monitoring is recommended. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of exemestane through its induction of CYP3A4 metabolism. For patients receiving exemestane with a potent CYP3A4 inducer, the recommended dose of exemestane is 50 mg daily after a meal. Caution and monitoring are advised. Fedratinib increases the plasma levels or effects of phenobarbital by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Dose adjustments of CYP2C19 substrates may be necessary. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of felbamate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of felodipine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while fenfluramine decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. Phenobarbital also reduces the plasma levels or effects of fenfluramine through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with drugs that increase serotonin may elevate the risk of serotonin syndrome. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of fentanyl with CYP3A4 inducers may lead to reduced fentanyl plasma concentrations, lack of efficacy, or withdrawal syndrome in physically dependent patients. After discontinuing a CYP3A4 inducer, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially prolonging therapeutic and adverse effects. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of fentanyl (intranasal, transdermal, and transmucosal) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 inducers may result in reduced fentanyl efficacy or withdrawal syndrome. Discontinuation of the inducer may increase fentanyl plasma concentrations, prolonging both therapeutic and adverse effects. Ferric maltol and phenobarbital may increase each other's levels through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Co-administration of ferric maltol with certain oral medications may reduce the bioavailability of either ferric maltol or the oral drugs. For drugs where reduced bioavailability may cause clinically significant effects, separate administration is advised, with the duration of separation depending on the absorption characteristics of the concomitant medication. Belladonna alkaloids and fesoterodine both reduce cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of fesoterodine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Fexinidazole increases the plasma levels or effects of phenobarbital by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and flavoxate both reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of flibanserin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers significantly decrease flibanserin systemic exposure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of fludrocortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids reduce the levels of fluphenazine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce fluphenazine levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism, while fluphenazine increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids via pharmacodynamic synergism. Phenobarbital and fluphenazine both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital and flurazepam both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Galantamine increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of fluticasone furoate and fluticasone inhaled by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while formoterol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of fosamprenavir and fosaprepitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of fosphenytoin by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of gefitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Increase gefitinib to 500 mg daily if co-administered with a strong CYP3A4 inducer. Resume the dose of 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the strong inducer. Phenobarbital decreases the plasma levels or effects of gentamicin by increasing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Givinostat increases the plasma levels or effects of phenobarbital by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Givinostat is a weak CYP3A4 inhibitor. Close monitoring is recommended when co-administered with orally administered CYP3A4-sensitive substrates, especially those with a narrow therapeutic index. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Co-administration with CYP3A4 and P-gp inducers may decrease glecaprevir/pibrentasvir plasma concentrations. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of glyburide by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Strong CYP2C9 inducers may increase glyburide metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and glycopyrrolate (including inhaled forms) both reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Gotu kola enhances the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism. This may increase CNS depression. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of guanfacine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers significantly reduce guanfacine plasma concentrations and elimination half-life. For ADHD patients, doubling the recommended dose of extended-release guanfacine may be considered. Guselkumab may alter CYP450 enzyme formation due to increased cytokine levels during chronic inflammation, potentially normalizing CYP450 enzyme activity. Upon initiation or discontinuation of guselkumab in patients receiving CYP450 substrates, particularly those with a narrow therapeutic index, monitor for therapeutic effects. Haloperidol increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Phenobarbital and haloperidol both increase sedation. Belladonna alkaloids reduce haloperidol levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Belladonna alkaloids also reduce haloperidol levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Phenobarbital decreases haloperidol levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hawthorn enhances the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and henbane both reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the effects of hemin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Drugs that increase delta-aminolevulinic acid synthetase may decrease hemin efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and homatropine both reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hops enhance the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergism, potentially increasing CNS depression. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Huperzine A increases cholinergic effects, while belladonna alkaloids decrease them. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of hydrocodone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised when discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers co-administered with hydrocodone, as plasma concentrations of hydrocodone may increase, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital and hydromorphone both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of hydroxyprogesterone caproate by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Hydroxyzine and phenobarbital both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and hyoscyamine (including spray forms) both reduce cholinergic effects. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital increases the effects of ifosfamide by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP2B6 inducers may increase ifosfamide metabolism to its active metabolite. Phenobarbital also increases ifosfamide toxicity by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, which may increase the formation of neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolites like chloroacetaldehyde. Close monitoring for toxicities and dose adjustments are recommended. Iloperidone increases the effects of belladonna alkaloids through pharmacodynamic synergism. Belladonna alkaloids reduce iloperidone levels through pharmacodynamic antagonism and inhibition of gastrointestinal absorption, which applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Phenobarbital and iloperidone both increase sedation. Phenobarbital reduces iloperidone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of imatinib by increasing P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and imipramine both reduce cholinergic effects. Phenobarbital reduces imipramine levels by inducing CYP1A2, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Phenobarbital and imipramine both increase sedation. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of indinavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing P-glycoprotein activity. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Belladonna alkaloids and ipratropium both reduce cholinergic effects. Due to poor systemic absorption of ipratropium, interaction is unlikely at recommended dosages. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital reduces the plasma levels or effects of iptacopan by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce iptacopan efficacy. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Phenobarbital increases sedation, while isoproterenol decreases sedation. The interaction effect is unclear, so caution is advised.
